page: Amazon Web Services r5.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Hardware caching consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache, with support for instruction extensions including AVX and AVX-512. System memory comprises 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Hardware specifications do not include bundled local storage or dedicated graphics processing units, necessitating reliance on remote storage volumes for system and data persistence. Network connectivity is configured with a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle tier for multi-core throughput, recording a stress-ng multi-core score of 27,099.03 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,476.0. Single-core performance occupies the lower quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,034.0. Uncached memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 103.04 GB/sec read and 46.96 GB/sec write throughput for large data blocks.

Resource efficiency is structured around high memory capacity per compute unit rather than peak single-threaded execution speed. Benchmark data shows consistent multi-threaded output in data-oriented tasks, reaching 10,868.77 on PassMark database operations and 25.97 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. The r5.8xlarge is engineered for memory-bound workloads, such as in-memory caching platforms, large relational databases requiring extensive buffer pools, data extraction and transformation jobs, and high-concurrency enterprise services.

Equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, the platform provides an 8.0 GB memory allocation per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, utilizing a 10 Gbps baseline network link for system interconnects. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits moderate multi-core throughput alongside lower single-core execution speed, balanced by uncached memory read bandwidth of 103.04 GB/sec and 25.97 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. By directing hardware resources primarily toward memory density, the r5.8xlarge is tailored for large-scale caching clusters, in-memory databases, and memory-intensive enterprise data processing.
